items.title: Cheaper flights home for Sarawak polls? Abang Johari fears bribery claims
items.summary: KUCHING, Nov 14 — The Sarawak caretaker administration is cautious about proposals for state-owned carrier AirBorneo Airways Sdn Bhd (AirBorneo) to offer special airfare discounts to voters travelling home for the 13th Sarawak Election, warning that such incentives could be misconstrued as electoral bribery. Caretaker Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg said that while the administration was open to facilitating travel for Sarawakians, any fare reductions must comply with election laws and avoid giving rise to allegations of vote-buying. He was responding to questions on whether the state government would consider directing AirBorneo to introduce additional airfare discounts to encourage out-of-state voters to return home and cast their ballots.

items.title: Melaka polls: 25 investigation papers referred to DPP
items.summary: MELAKA: Police have referred 25 investigation papers involving various offences during the 2026 Melaka state election to the Deputy Public Prosecutor's Office. Melaka police chief Datuk Dzulkhairi Mukhtar said police had received 37 reports and opened 28 investigation papers so far. Dzulkhairi said voting at all 240 polling centres, involving 1,213 channels, was proceeding peacefully, with no incidents reported as of 9am.

items.title: Melaka polls: 28.8 per cent turnout recorded as of 11.05am
items.summary: MELAKA: A total of 28.8 per cent of ordinary eligible voters in the Melaka election had cast their ballots as of 11.05am today. According to the Election Commission's (EC) real-time Voter Turnout Monitoring (VTO) dashboard, 194,871 voters had cast their ballots by then. The EC is targeting a 70 per cent turnout for the election, which sees 79 candidates contesting 28 seats.

items.title: Anwar receives 11 outstanding asnaf pupils from Kinabatangan who achieved national, international success
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim yesterday received a visit from 11 outstanding asnaf pupils from Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Singgah Manis in Kinabatangan, Sabah, accompanied by seven of their teachers, at Kompleks Seri Perdana. In a Facebook post, Anwar said he was impressed by the perseverance of the pupils and teachers, who had achieved various successes at state, national and international levels despite coming from a rural school. Anwar also expressed his appreciation to the school’s teachers for their commitment to educating, guiding and instilling confidence in the pupils to reach greater heights.

items.title: Sarawak school alert leads to arrest of palm worker, 28, after Year Six girl found pregnant
items.summary: KABONG, Nov 14 — Sarawak police have arrested a 28-year-old man after a 12-year-old Year Six pupil was found to be pregnant, Berita Harian reported last night. The case came to light when the girl’s mother took her to school to inform the management of the pregnancy, Saratok district police chief Deputy Superintendent Mathew Manggie said. Initial investigations found that the suspect, an oil palm plantation worker, had known the girl since mid-2025, Mathew said.

items.title: Melaka polls: Student spends RM700 on air tickets to cast first vote
items.summary: KOTA MELAKA: A 20-year-old university student spent RM700 on return flight tickets from Sarawak to Melaka so she could fulfil her responsibility as a first-time voter in the 16th Melaka election today. Ashira Dania Mohd Hairun, a first-year Social Sciences student at Universiti Malaysia Sarawak (Unimas), returned to her hometown in Taman Seri Duyong 2 here to cast her ballot. She said she was excited to vote for the first time, as it was her first opportunity to choose her elected representative.

items.title: Minister: Govt exploring Sijil Turath Malaysia implementation next year to give pondok students university pathway
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 14 — The government is exploring the implementation of the Sijil Turath Malaysia, expected to be introduced next year, to give official recognition to pondok and turath students and open pathways for them to pursue university studies and build careers. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the move follows Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s announcement when tabling Budget 2027, which also includes the establishment of the Malaysian Pondok and Turath Advisory Council. “So we want to see how best to develop this Sijil Turath Malaysia.

items.title: Melaka polls: Uncle Wong, 88, cycles to polling centre after 3am start
items.summary: MELAKA: Eager to fulfil his duty as a voter, Vong Fook Hoi, better known as Uncle Wong, 88, woke up about 3am and cycled to the polling centre at SK Seri Duyong here today. I could not sleep last night either. I go everywhere by bicycle," he said after casting his ballot for the Duyong seat here today.

items.title: Trump not expected to raise Alice Huang case with China's Xi
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump is not expected to discuss with Chinese President Xi Jinping the case involving a businesswoman whose ties to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang raised national security concerns, US officials said on Friday. A second US official added: "I don't expect the president to raise it, the Alice Huang issue." Alice Huang could not be reached.

items.title: Melaka polls: Wheelchair no barrier to 70-year-old Yusuf fulfilling his voting duty [WATCH]
items.summary: MELAKA: Being wheelchair-bound did not stop 70-year-old Yusuf Taib from fulfilling his responsibility as a voter in the Melaka election today. Yusuf, who has been voting since before Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad first became prime minister in 1981, said his enthusiasm for exercising his democratic right had never faded. "I have been voting since before Mahathir became prime minister.

items.title: AirBorneo takes off for Jakarta: Kuching direct flights from RM399
items.summary: KUCHING, Nov 14 — Sarawak’s state-owned carrier AirBorneo Airways Sdn Bhd (AirBorneo) has launched direct flights between Kuching and Jakarta, establishing a new air link between Sarawak and Indonesia’s capital. The inaugural flight, MY396, departed Kuching International Airport yesterday and arrived at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport Terminal 3 to a traditional water salute, completing the journey in under two hours. AirBorneo chief executive officer Megat Ardian Aminuddin said Jakarta was the airline’s first destination in Indonesia and its third jet route since services began in July.

items.title: Melaka polls: Woman flies home from Australia to vote with elderly parents
items.summary: MELAKA: Distance proved no barrier to civic duty as 38-year-old Wong Chea Fann returned from Australia this morning to cast her ballot alongside her elderly parents at SJK (C) Malim for the Kesidang state seat. Wong, together with her parents, Wong Heng Hoe, 79, and Lee Cheng Tee, 70, were among the early voters who arrived at the polling centre at 9am. "It's quite exciting, but most importantly, my parents arrived safely to vote," she said.

items.title: US reopens airspace after nationwide flight halt, rules out cyberattack
items.summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told a late-night briefing at the White House that US airspace was now "opened up," while warning it would take time for the travel chaos to clear. "At 8.15 tonight Eastern Time, we've opened up the airspace," Duffy said. "Our switches, our routers actually got overloaded with data, and they went down," Duffy said.

items.title: Civic duty knows no bounds: Visually impaired voter travels from Ipoh to vote in Melaka
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 14 — A 23-year-old visually impaired voter travelled from Ipoh, Perak, to Melaka today to exercise his democratic right, making the long journey to fulfil his civic duty. Muhammad Adam Iskandar Muhammad Rayme, a voter in the Bukit Katil state constituency, said this was his second time voting, having first cast his ballot at the age of 19 with his mother accompanying him. — Bernama

items.title: MB: Johor govt hopes filling of posts at Hospital Pasir Gudang can be expedited as nurses, specialists in short supply
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 14 — The Johor State Government hopes the filling of posts at Hospital Pasir Gudang (HPG) can be expedited to ensure sufficient manpower in line with the hospital’s expanding service capacity. Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said 1,276 of the 2,271 posts allocated to HPG had been filled as of November 6, or 56 per cent. “The Johor State Government will continue to champion manpower needs and the welfare of healthcare workers to provide the best healthcare services for Bangsa Johor, InsyaAllah,” he said in a Facebook post.

items.title: She knew and chose silence: Kuching mother gets five years’ jail for allowing teen daughter’s sexual abuse
items.summary: KUCHING, Nov 14 — A 52-year-old woman was sentenced to five years’ imprisonment by the Sessions Court here for allowing her teenage daughter to be sexually abused by her 77-year-old grand-uncle and failing to lodge a police report despite having knowledge about the incident. Judge Noorhisham Mohd Jaafar imposed the sentence after the woman pleaded guilty to an offence framed under Section 31(1)(b) of the Child Act 2001. Noorhisham also ordered her to undergo rehabilitative counselling throughout her imprisonment period under Section 26(1) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act (SOACA) 2017.

items.title: Roque: Asean must turn economic commitments into gains for businesses, people
items.summary: MANILA: Asean must back its economic integration plans with clear milestones and consistent implementation to deliver benefits for businesses, consumers and workers, Philippine Trade and Industry Secretary Cristina Roque said. She said the Asean Economic Community (AEC) Strategic Plan 2026-2030 required effective coordination, while unfinished priority economic deliverables under the Philippines' chairmanship needed to be completed and sustained beyond this year. [[nid:1577284]] Roque outlined three priorities for the council's discussions: reviewing the Philippines' priority economic deliverables, advancing implementation of the AEC Strategic Plan 2026–2030 and finalising reports and outcomes for the upcoming Asean summit.

items.title: Penang Education Dept to probe allegation that teacher slapped, pinched SPM candidate
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM, Nov 14 — The Penang State Education Department is investigating allegations that a teacher repeatedly slapped and pinched an Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) candidate, causing bruises, and verbally humiliated the student at a school here. Penang Education Department director Mohamad Dziauddin Mat Saad said the department received a complaint regarding the incident and instructed the District Education Office to conduct an investigation and submit recommendations on further action and resolution. “The district education office also met with the student and the student’s family this evening.

items.title: Flood evacuees increase in Selangor, drop in Perak
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — The number of flood evacuees seeking shelter at temporary relief centres (PPS) increased in Selangor but declined in Perak as of 8am today. In SELANGOR, flood evacuee numbers at seven temporary relief centres in Kuala Selangor rose to 1,498 people from 402 families this morning, up from 1,373 people from 369 families yesterday evening. Meanwhile, in PERAK, the number of flood evacuees in Hilir Perak district fell to 265 people from 74 families, down from 274 people from 79 families yesterday evening.

items.title: Ab Rauf and Adam Adli cast ballots as Melaka heads to polls
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 14 — Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh cast his vote for the 16th Melaka state election at 8.38am today. The Melaka Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman, who is also the incumbent of Tanjung Bidara state constituency, arrived to vote at Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Jeram in Masjid Tanah, Alor Gajah, accompanied by his wife, Datin Seri Zuriyah Ab Aziz, who also cast her vote at the same location. Higher Education Deputy Minister Adam Adli Abd Halim votes in the 16th Melaka State Election at Sekolah Kebangsaan Demang Hussin November 14, 2026.

items.title: ICC closes original Afghanistan war crimes investigation
items.summary: ISTANBUL: Judges at the International Criminal Court (ICC) have ordered the formal closure of the court's original investigation into alleged crimes in Afghanistan, which included allegations against US troops, Anadolu Ajansi reported. A separate investigation into alleged crimes by the Taliban since August 2021 will continue. The Chamber also noted that, although the investigation was authorised to cover alleged crimes committed in Afghanistan from May 1, 2003, and conflict-related crimes in other ICC member states from July 1, 2002, the prosecution had submitted only a limited number of applications under Article 58, all concerning the separate Situation in Afghanistan II, or the alleged crimes in Afghanistan since August 2021.

items.title: Gunung Kanthan limestone notch at critical risk of collapse, expert warns
items.summary: Emeritus Professor Datuk Dr Ibrahim Komoo said the formation was unsuitable for permanent habitation as it contained suspended limestone blocks without firm support. This process had weakened the natural cement holding the limestone blocks together through water seepage, increasing the risk of collapse. "The condition at Gunung Kanthan is critical because limestone blocks are hanging without firm support.

items.title: Man gets 12 months' jail, RM250,000 fine for Quran desecration in Pahang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — A man was sentenced to 12 months in prison and fined RM250,000 by the Kuantan Sessions Court in Pahang for desecrating the Quran and posting grossly offensive content on social media in February. The court ordered the prison sentence to take effect from November 12, with an additional 12 months’ imprisonment if he fails to pay the fine. As a result, the accused began serving his prison sentence yesterday.

items.title: No bomb threat: Man arrested after suspicious suitcase near KLCC sparks road closure, social media frenzy
items.summary: Dang Wangi district police chief ACP Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said police received information about the discovery of the object at 7.17pm. He said following this, a team comprising personnel from the Bomb Disposal Unit, K9 Unit and Kuala Lumpur Police Forensics Unit was dispatched to the scene to conduct checks and secure the area. Members of the public with information related to the incident can contact the Kuala Lumpur Police Hotline at 03-2146 0522, the Dang Wangi district police headquarters control centre at 03-2600 2222, or any nearby police station.

items.title: Woman found strangled in Banting, police arrest son to aid probe
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 14 — A woman in her 50s was found dead, believed to have been strangled, at a house in Banting, Kuala Langat, yesterday. Kuala Langat district police chief Supt Mohd Akmalrizal Radzi said police were alerted to the incident at about 1 pm. Members of the public with information about the incident are urged to contact the Kuala Langat District police headquarters operations room at 03-31872222 or the nearest police station.

items.title: Nearly 97,000 foreigners arrested for crimes since 2024
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Authorities arrested 96,844 foreigners for various criminal offences nationwide between 2024 and September this year, reflecting a year-on-year upward trend. Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the total comprised 33,136 arrests in 2024, before rising to 36,740 in 2025. "From January to September this year, 26,968 arrests of foreigners involved in criminal offences were recorded.

items.title: Three houses damaged in Nibong Tebal pre-dawn blaze
items.summary: NIBONG TEBAL: Three single-storey houses were damaged in an early morning fire at Kampung Baru Sungai Kecil today. Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations John Sagun Francis said the department received an emergency call at 4.10am. John said the fire destroyed about 90 per cent of the second house, 60 per cent of the first, and 1 per cent of the third.

items.title: MCMC warns public over scams impersonating its officers after 61 arrested in Selangor
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 14 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) takes a serious view of the misuse of its officers’ names and identities to deceive the public, particularly for fraudulent purposes. “The MCMC views seriously any misuse of its officers’ names and identities to deceive the public, especially in fraudulent activities that could threaten public safety and undermine public trust,” it said. The MCMC advised the public to remain vigilant when receiving calls or messages from individuals claiming to be its officers.

items.title: Flood evacuees increase in Selangor, drop in Perak
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The number of flood evacuees seeking shelter at temporary relief centres (PPS) increased in Selangor but declined in Perak as of 8am today. In Selangor , flood evacuee numbers at seven temporary relief centres in Kuala Selangor rose to 1,498 people from 402 families this morning, up from 1,373 people from 369 families yesterday evening. Meanwhile, in Perak , the number of flood evacuees in Hilir Perak district fell to 265 people from 74 families, down from 274 people from 79 families yesterday evening.

items.title: No free pass for foreigners who break the law, IGP says as arrests since 2024 near 97,000
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Police will take firm action against any violation of the law and criminal conduct involving foreigners in Malaysia, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail has said. He said 96,844 foreign nationals were arrested for various crimes from 2024 to September 2026, based on Criminal Investigation Department (CID) statistics. “PDRM will take firm action against any form of violation of the law and criminal conduct involving foreigners in Malaysia,” Mohd Khalid said in a statement in Malay today, using the abbreviation for the Royal Malaysia Police.

items.title: Anwar to lead Malaysian delegation at 49th Asean Summit in Manila, says envoy
items.summary: MANILA, Nov 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is scheduled to arrive in Manila tomorrow to lead the Malaysian delegation to the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits from November 15 to 17. Abdul Malik said Anwar will be accompanied by his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, and Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani. On Sunday, the Prime Minister is scheduled to attend the plenary and retreat sessions of the 49th Asean Summit, as well as Asean leaders’ engagement sessions with the Asean Inter-Parliamentary Assembly (AIPA), the Asean Business Advisory Council (Asean-BAC) and Asean youth.

items.title: Asean leaders to review implementation of Myanmar Five-Point Consensus, chart way forward
items.summary: MANILA: Asean leaders will review the implementation of the Five-Point Consensus (5PC) on Myanmar at the 49th Asean Summit in Manila and adopt a decision to guide the bloc's future engagement with the country, Philippine Secretary of Foreign Affairs Theresa P. Lazaro said. She said the document, titled the Asean Leaders' Review and Decision on the Implementation of the Five-Point Consensus, would take stock of developments in Myanmar and assess progress in implementing the 5PC since the previous review. Lazaro said Myanmar had established an Asean Affairs Committee.

items.title: Over 500 tourism operators under scrutiny, dozens offering umrah packages
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: More than 500 companies and individuals suspected of operating tourism businesses without valid licences are being monitored by the Tourism, Arts and Culture Ministry, with dozens offering umrah packages. The offences identified include violations of Section 21, involving the provision of tour guide services, and Subsection 5(2), which prohibits individuals or companies from operating tourism businesses without a valid licence. It said 12 entities had also been issued compounds for conducting tourism activities without valid licences.

items.title: Cast your ballots early before it rains, Ab Rauf tells Melaka voters [WATCH]
items.summary: MASJID TANAH: Caretaker Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh has urged voters to head to polling centres early today, citing forecasts of rain in the afternoon. The Melaka Barisan Nasional chairman said voters should take advantage of the morning hours to cast their ballots, although arrangements had been made to assist them should it rain later. On the voting process, Ab Rauf said he was satisfied with the arrangements made by Election Commission personnel, describing the process as orderly and convenient for voters.

items.title: PKFZ says Speedmatrix didn’t sign, Port Klang land lease won’t go ahead
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Speedmatrix Sdn Bhd’s proposed lease of land in Port Klang will not proceed after the company did not sign a letter of offer that has since expired, Port Klang Free Zone Sdn Bhd (PKFZ) said today. In a statement today, PKFZ said it was responding to recent reports concerning Speedmatrix. PKFZ said Speedmatrix sought to lease a parcel of land within the free zone in July.

items.title: Melaka polls: 9.42 per cent turnout recorded as of 9am
items.summary: MELAKA: A total of 9.42 per cent of ordinary voters in the Melaka election had cast their ballots as of 9am today. According to the Election Commission's real-time Voter Turnout Monitoring (VTO) dashboard, 64,668 voters had cast their ballots by that time. The EC is targeting a 70 per cent turnout for the state election, which sees 79 candidates contesting 28 seats.

items.title: Anwar extends condolences to former deputy minister Zahidi's family
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has extended his condolences to the family of former Communications and Multimedia deputy minister Datuk Zahidi Zainul Abidin, who passed away yesterday. In a Facebook post, Anwar prayed that Allah SWT would forgive the deceased’s sins and shower his soul with mercy. “May his family be granted strength and remain steadfast in facing this great trial,” he said.

items.title: MetMalaysia: Wind convergence to bring thunderstorms, heavy rain to most peninsular states from Nov 15 to 17
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are expected in most states in Peninsular Malaysia from November 15 to 17, according to the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia). “This situation could bring thunderstorms accompanied by heavy rain and strong winds over a longer duration in most states in Peninsular Malaysia,” he said in a statement posted on MetMalaysia’s Facebook page. In a related development, MetMalaysia has issued a thunderstorm, heavy rain and strong wind warning for five states until 11 o’clock last night.

items.title: Anwar to lead Malaysian delegation at 49th Asean Summit in Manila
items.summary: MANILA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is scheduled to arrive here today to lead the Malaysian delegation to the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits, which run from tomorrow until Tuesday. Abdul Malik said Anwar will be accompanied by his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, alongside Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan and Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani. [[nid:1577232]] "Tomorrow, the prime minister is scheduled to attend the 49th Asean Summit, comprising the plenary and retreat sessions, as well as three engagement sessions with the Asean Inter-Parliamentary Assembly (AIPA), the Asean Business Advisory Council (Asean-BAC) and Asean Youth.

items.title: US recalls over 720,000 BMW vehicles over fire risk, urges owners to park outside
items.summary: NEW JERSEY: United States (US) safety regulators have advised owners of 720,796 BMW vehicles to park outside and away from buildings as an electrical fault could cause a fire, Anadolu Ajansi (AA) reported, citing recall documents. "Owners are advised to park their vehicles outside and away from structures until the recall remedy is completed," the agency said in a Nov 12 letter acknowledging BMW's recall. The recall covers certain 2012–2016 3 Series, 5 Series and Z4 vehicles; 2012–2015 X1s; 2013–2017 X3s; 2015–2018 X4s; and 2016–2018 X5 xDrive40e models.

items.title: PM urges Melaka voters to reject exploiters of religion, corrupt individuals
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has urged the people of Melaka to use their ballots in the state election tomorrow to reject those who exploit religion for political gain, as well as individuals involved in corruption. “Tomorrow, the people of Melaka have an opportunity to send a strong message through the ballot box. Save Melaka.

items.title: Trump, Xi, Putin to hold historic meeting in China: White House
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping will hold the first ever three-way meeting between the leaders of the United States, Russia and China at a summit in Shenzhen next week, the White House said Friday. Trump wants to talk about reducing nuclear arsenals at the trilateral talks on Thursday and is also set to bring up his war in Iran – but he is not expected to discuss Russia's war in Ukraine, US officials said. This proliferation, President Trump believes, is very dangerous," Wales said.

items.title: Former Communications and Multimedia deputy minister Zahidi Zainul Abidin dies at 65
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 14 — Former Communications and Multimedia deputy minister Datuk Zahidi Zainul Abidin died yesterday and was laid to rest at the Bayan Lepas Islamic Cemetery after Isyak prayers last night. News of his passing was shared by former Perlis Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Shahidan Kassim, who extended his condolences to the deceased’s family. In a Facebook post, Shahidan, who is the Member of Parliament for Arau, said he was deeply saddened by his friend’s passing.

items.title: Bus, container truck collide head-on in India, killing 23
items.summary: NEW DELHI: A head-on collision between a container truck and a passenger bus killed at least 23 people, including three children, in eastern India on Friday, a police official told AFP. "The total number of casualties is 23," said Swapneel Deka, the local district police chief. Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said he was "deeply distressed by the tragic accident."

items.title: Melaka votes today: 79 candidates seek mandate from 675,166 electors
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 14 — After the Melaka State Election campaign ended at midnight last night, the power to choose now shifts to 675,166 ordinary voters who will determine the fate of 79 candidates competing for 28 state assembly seats today. In the 15th Melaka State Election held in November 2021, BN won 21 out of 28 state seats, with PH (five) and PN (two). Get the latest news on the 16th Melaka State Election at https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/ .

items.title: Negeri Sembilan MB moves to back Tuanku Muhriz and avert government shutdown, says source
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has taken steps this week to affirm the status of Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as Yang di-Pertuan Besar, in a development that may finally see an end to the state’s seven-month-long constitutional crisis. But he needs the consent of Tuanku Muhriz for the state assembly to meet. A source told Malay Mail that Ismail met earlier this week with Tan Sri Syed Danial Syed Ahmad, the Keeper of the Rulers’ Seal, and presented him with a letter withdrawing objections to Tuanku Muhriz’s position as state ruler.

items.title: Melaka polls: From morning jog straight to polling station for 80-year-old voter
items.summary: MELAKA: At 80, retired civil servant Jusop Karim remains committed to exercising his right to vote, making a stop at SK Seri Duyong here after his morning jog and breakfast today. Jusop said he had decided to visit the polling centre before proceeding with his other activities for the day. On the contest in Duyong, Jusop described the competition among the candidates as close, based on the information he had received.

items.title: Melaka polls: Ab Rauf arrives at SK Jeram to cast his vote [WATCH]
items.summary: MASJID TANAH: Caretaker Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh arrived at SK Jeram here about 8.30am to cast his vote in the Melaka election today. Ab Rauf, who is also the incumbent Tanjung Bidara assemblyman, arrived at the polling centre wearing a batik shirt. Tanjung Bidara has 15,003 registered voters.

items.title: Melaka polls: 240 polling centres across state open simultaneously at 8am for 675,166 Melaka voters
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 14 — A total of 240 ordinary polling centres, with 1,213 polling streams, for the 16th Melaka state election opened simultaneously at 8am today, allowing voters cast their ballots and elect a state government for the next term. The Election Commission (EC) said a total of 675,166 ordinary voters were eligible to cast their ballots to elect representatives for the 28 state constituencies, with voter turnout expected to reach 70 per cent. For the latest updates on the 16th Melaka State Election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/.

items.title: Melaka polls: Elderly couple up at 5am to cast votes
items.summary: Liew said they had set off after breakfast, with the polling centre about 2km from their home. The father of three said he wanted to complete the voting process early as he had to open his shop in Masjid Tanah about 9am. He said arriving early had become a habit whenever elections were held.

items.title: Ex-Nvidia CEO misled top lawyer on affair with Chinese businesswoman, sources say
items.summary: SAN FRANCISCO: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang misled several of the company's leaders, including general counsel Tim Teter and chief marketing officer Alison Wagonfeld, about the nature of his relationship with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, with whom he had an affair, according to two people familiar with the matter and internal correspondence reviewed by Reuters. Jensen Huang and Alice Huang share a last name but are not related. The New York Times earlier this week reported Huang also had an extramarital relationship with an Nvidia employee, and Reuters reported on Thursday that Huang had another intimate relationship with a different Nvidia employee.

items.title: MCMC warns of scammers after 61 held for impersonating officers
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The public have been advised to verify the identities of those claiming to be Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) officers before sharing personal information or making financial transactions. "The public is urged to verify such claims through official channels before sharing personal information or making any financial transactions," it said in a statement. The MCMC said such impersonation could threaten public safety and undermine public trust.

items.title: Prisons Dept: Najib’s nearly eight-hour outing on Friday was not only for prayers, included hospital check-up and counselling
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — The Prisons Department has clarified that former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s nearly eight-hour absence from his house arrest residence on Friday was not solely for Friday prayers, as earlier reported. According to the department, Najib attended a follow-up medical appointment at the orthopaedic department of Hospital Kuala Lumpur. The department said he also attended a Quran study session with an ustaz from the Islamic Development Department at Kajang Prison.

items.title: Man arrested over suspicious suitcase near KLCC
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police arrested a 40-year-old man over a suspicious suitcase found at a bus stop near Suria KLCC in Jalan Ampang last night. Dang Wangi district police chief assistant commissioner Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said police received information about the discovery of the object at 7.17pm. Those with information can contact Kuala Lumpur police hotline at 03-2146 0522, Dang Wangi police headquarters control centre at 03-2600 2222, or the nearest police station.

items.title: Melaka polls: 240 polling centres across state open simultaneously at 8am [WATCH]
items.summary: MELAKA: A total of 240 ordinary polling centres, with 1,213 polling streams, for the 16th Melaka state election opened simultaneously at 8am today, allowing voters cast their ballots and elect a state government for the next term. The Election Commission (EC) said a total of 675,166 ordinary voters were eligible to cast their ballots to elect representatives for the 28 state constituencies, with voter turnout expected to reach 70 per cent. In the 15th Melaka State Election held on Nov 20, 2021, BN won 21 of the 28 state seats, while PH secured five and PN two.

items.title: Amazon fires: Brazil's Pará state declares 120-day emergency amid severe drought
items.summary: BRASÍLIA: A northern Brazilian state has declared an environmental state of emergency due to hundreds of forest fires in the Amazon basin amid a severe drought linked to the El Nino climate phenomenon. Nearly 700 fires were active in the last 48 hours. In 2024, the Brazilian Amazon recorded a record number of forest fires.

items.title: Melaka polls become test of Najib house arrest row, with GE16 battle lines emerging
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Melaka voters head to the polls today for a state election that began as a contest over development, governance and political alliances, but has become increasingly dominated by the controversy surrounding former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest. Meanwhile, Pakatan Harapan (PH) has used the controversy as a rallying point to challenge Umno and mobilise voters unhappy with the decision. Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim (on stage centre) stumps for Pakatan Harapan at the coalition’s grand finale ceramah in Bukit Baru, Melaka on November 12, 2026.

items.title: Designing the money part of Malaysia’s long-term care system: Economists share what to look out for
items.summary: So what can Malaysia consider when designing a long-term care scheme? Long-term care system: Tax-funded or insurance? World Bank senior economist Matthew Dornan said there is “no easy answer” for how Malaysia would fund its long-term care system.

items.title: PKR leaders slam Hadi over remarks comparing Muslim, non-Muslim leaders, question PAS ties with MCA, Gerakan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — Several PKR leaders have criticised PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang over his remarks comparing Muslim and non-Muslim leaders, warning that religious sentiments should not be used to divide Malaysians for political gain. PKR vice-president Datuk Chang Lih Kang said political differences should be debated based on policies and solutions to people’s problems rather than religious sentiments. He described Abdul Hadi’s remarks during a Melaka state election campaign event yesterday as deeply disappointing, saying statements that hurt religious sensitivities and fuel tensions would only harm the country.

items.title: HKL monitors cop after successful hand reattachment following Kepong machete attack
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — The Ministry of Health (MOH), through the Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL), is closely monitoring the recovery of a policeman whose hand was reattached following an attack on Wednesday (November 11). HKL director Datuk Dr Harikrishna K. Ragavan Nair said the policeman was referred to the hospital for specialist treatment and immediately taken to the Main Operating Theatre for surgery after thorough examination and assessment by a team of specialists. “The surgery was led by HKL Upper Limb and Microsurgery subspecialists Dr R. Allan Ravi and Dr Aziz Sabbir Husain, in collaboration with the entire HKL Upper Limb and Microsurgery Unit team and the anaesthesiology team,” he said in a statement here today.
